utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I went to interrogation, maybe an hour before that, I was moved to another room which was second to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were held in the end room until, perhaps, an hour before your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were still in the end room on that day, did you see Hakija Elezovic taken out from that room for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was taken from the small room, not from that other one on the right, and while I was in the small room, Hakija was taken to interrogation from the small room, the one straight ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he brought back to that room? Did you see him brought back to that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him taken out once again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were transferred to the second room on the right of the white house building, was Zuhdija Turkanovic also transferred to that room with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken to the administrative restaurant building to be interrogated that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the administrative building but not to the restaurant, but to the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back from that interrogation, as you approached the white house, did a guard call out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were on your way back to the white house after your interrogation, did a guard call out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that guard when he called out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was on the first corner towards the administration building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first corner of what building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the first corner next to the building where I was going to be interrogated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were going back to the white house, the guard was located at the corner of what building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the corner of the building of the white house, to the first corner which was closest to me on my way back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the guard called out to you, did you go to the guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you walked to the guard, did you recognise or did you see other men with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many other men did you see with that guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some four or five people there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Dusan Tadic, Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you got there to where that guard was standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I approached him he ordered me to walk away from them some 10 metres and sit down on the grass and to turn towards, to face them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This guard who ordered you to do that, did you know this guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you were ordered to go and sit on the grass and turn toward them about 10 metres away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, to face them because they were facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you sat there 10 metres away you were facing these men by the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then after you sat down 10 metres away from these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That guard that ordered me to do this, he asked me where I was from and how old I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the guards, that is, the guard who was standing next to him, ran towards me, quickly towards me, and when he approached me, when he was about two metres from me, he jumped at me as if he was going to kick me, but he did not. He just jumped over me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This guard that ran towards you as though he were going to kick you and then jumped over you, what did he look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wore a camouflage uniform and he had, as we say, wavy blond hair, not completely wavy, but wavy-ish blond hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These other men, including Dule Tadic, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They also wore camouflage uniforms, except for the first guard who had called me out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that guard wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wore a blue short sleeved shirt and trousers, I think, were also camouflage but I am not completely sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then after this guard jumped over you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guard who had called me out again asked me -- in fact, he told me, did I say that I was from Trnopolje, and I said, "Yes". Then he told me to get up and to follow him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you followed him where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was walking in front of me. I was walking behind him and we turned the corner of the white house and found ourselves on the other side of the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went from one side of the white house to the other, did you go behind the white house or did you go in front of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went from the front where the door was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are now on the other side of the white house, on the hangar side of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not towards the hangar. On the side of that building, on the opposite, there was nothing there. The hangar was straight from the side of the house where the door was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, if you looked at the white house you are now on the left side of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you asking him to point where it was?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we are looking -- if we are observing the house towards the door from that side, then I was to the left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to have him mark different areas a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you reached the left side of the white house, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the corner which was the other corner, the other side of the left side, when I arrived there, there were four bodies which were put one on top of the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then when you saw these four bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guard who had brought me here told me, because these bodies were turned facing down, facing the ground, that I should turn them over so that their faces would be up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you turned them over, did the bodies fall from off of each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that the first body that was at the top I turned to the right and the second to the left, so that the remaining two bodies I just turned over, because there was room for the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these four bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Salih Elezovic, I recognised Senad Sivac, Ramadanovic (sic) Redzep and Nedzed Causevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you recognised Senad Sivac, do you know what his occupation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was -- he worked as a veterinarian in Kozarac so he was a veterinarian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was from Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether his first name was Senad or Sejad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible, could be Sejad or Senad. I am not sure now, but one of the two, it is for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a veterinarian from Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men that you saw, to your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How had you known these men before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Salih and Arslanovic. So Arslanovic and Elezovic I knew because they lived in the same hamlet where I was born. Salih otherwise is a relative and a neighbour and Arslanovic was a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Sivac before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was -- because in that region there were not many veterinarians, I even remember him coming once to our house. I think it was in connection with some disease, some animal disease.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know Mr. Causevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him while we were being transferred from Keraterm to Omarska and he was together with me in the small room in the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any injuries on these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Elezovic I saw that under his chin he had a wound which was made, I do not know, which was either a bullet or a stab wound. I do not know now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you turned these men over, what did the guard ask you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me whether I knew these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you reply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told him that I did not know them, even though I did know them but I told him that I did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like to break at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 p.m.) (Short Adjournment) (4.20 p.m.).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Hodzic, you had indicated that you knew Mr. Arslanovic because he was a neighbour of yours, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arslanovic's first name was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Redzep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was Redzep Arslanovic that was one of the bodies that you saw on the side of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the guard had asked you if you recognised any of these men and you said no. Why did you tell him no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, I do not know why that was my reply, but it was my reply. I, nevertheless, said that I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there on the side of the white house, did you take the shoes from any of the dead men there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you take the shoes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Elezovic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you took the shoes from Salih Elezovic did you put the shoes on there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I had them in my hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after you took the shoes and had them in your hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took the shoes and I returned from those bodies some two metres backwards, so that I was standing right up at the wall of the white house, and then a guard approached, the guard who had brought me there. The two of them talked there about something. At that moment the one who had brought me there turned towards me and sent me in, he said, "Get lost, scram, beat it, inside", whereupon I turned and ran to the white house and went in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were on the side of the white house where the four bodies were located, what were you concentrating on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the while my eyes and my thoughts, my eyes were focused on those bodies and all my thoughts were focused on those bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look around at any other area back there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the position you were at on the side of the white house, would you have been able to see behind the white house if you had looked there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, well, as I was turning the bodies over I would turn my head just a little bit to see if there was anything behind the white house. Had there been anything, I would have seen it certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you look at the area behind the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think I have looked there, no, not once did I look behind the white house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went back into the white house what room did you go into?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The room that was the second room to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you entered the white house, you went back to the second room on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, that evening or that night, did you hear the sound of any trucks near the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day did you see those four bodies on the side of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic as you stood at the corner of the white house near those men, how far away from you was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whilst I was sitting on the grass, it could have been some 10 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were standing at the corner of the white house looking at those men, how far away would Dule Tadic have been from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you sat about 10 metres away from Dule Tadic and the other men, did you have a clear view of Dule Tadic or was your view obstructed by anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could see him clearly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what he was wearing that day? You have indicated a camouflage uniform. Do you recall the colours in that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those colours were mostly brown, green, mixed with a coffee colour. As far as I can recall, they are those typical military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall on that day whether he had any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe he had not shaved for two or three days, so it was about a millimetre stubble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask you at this time to go around to this model in front of you and to point to the end room you were in and also to attach some pieces of paper to the model. What I would like you to do is to take your headphones off here, then when you come around to the model, to put the headphones on that are located on the bench in front of you. If you could come up to my direction a little, please? If you can look into the white house and if you can put that pointer in the room in the end where you stayed until the day of your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a number in that room, if you could tell us what that number is and when you do that please turn around and speak to the microphone behind you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is room A5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could come a little bit toward me, please, so the Judges can have an unobstructed view? I am going to ask you to place certain pieces of paper on the model. First, I would like you to place the letter "W" on the model where you were when the guard first called you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would please place a "W1" in the position you were as you stood at the right corner of the white house, the corner near the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could place the letter "T" where Dule Tadic was when you saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if you could place "W2" where you were as you sat 10 metres away from Dule and Tadic and the other guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if we look at the other side of the white house, if you could place the letter "B" where you saw the four bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could return to your seat, please? Mr. Hodzic you have indicated that when you returned to the white house you returned to the second room on the left. When you returned to this room did you see Zuhdija Turkanovic in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his condition when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in a very poor state. He was beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when you saw your friend there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was, because of all that pain he simply asked for help, not from anyone in particular, but he was crying, "Help me", and at that moment I tried to comfort him telling him that everything would be all right. I even put his head on my feet, on my legs, but after some 10 minutes or so he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Zuhdija Turkanovic died, did other detainees take his body from the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how soon after he died his body was taken from the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How soon after your friend died did the detainees take his body from the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe some 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your recollection, did you see Hakija Elezovic in Omarska after you saw the body of his son, Salih?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him after that. Since he was taken for interrogation for a second time, I have not seen him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken from Omarska to Manjaca camp on 6th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way to Manjaca, do you recall women and children yelling at the buses as you passed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they yelling at the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The children and women were yelling, "Why are you driving them away, kill them, why are you driving them there?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you held at Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 6th August until 18th December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Karlovac or, to be more precise, to Croatia, to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the attack on Kozarac on 24th May, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of any organised anti-Serb resistance group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the attack on Kozarac on 24th May, did you become a member of any such group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, as a result of attacks in opstina Prijedor and the camps that were established there, are any members of your family missing or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My uncle was killed, and the son of another uncle has also been killed, and of my family proper, that is, mother and father, brothers and sisters, no.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Cross-Examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, it seems that you have not spent much time with Dusko Tadic before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He is not a man with whom you sat at a cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have not been into his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He has not been to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have spent no time in his company on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you only, in fact, seen Dusko Tadic two or three times at his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would see him when I happened to be there. I do not remember how many times exactly, but when I came there I saw him because that coffee bar is not particularly big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you recollect this day in Omarska when you had to move those bodies by the white house, can you remember the description of the man you called Dusko Tadic, what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see Mr. Tadic when I was turning the bodies, but when I was on the other side of the white house, and when I saw him there, he was wearing a camouflage uniform, had an automatic rifle, as far as I can recall, across his right shoulder. He was -- he had more weight and, as far as I could see, he was, he had, he had -- he was somewhat tanned, probably from sun or something, as compared with the last time I saw him. The last time I saw him he was somewhat paler in the face, that is, before the war, before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did his face look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have said, he was somewhat tanned. He must have been exposed to the sun somewhere, so that is why he was -- his complexion was slightly darker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was not the face of this man red as if he had some kind of facial irritation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he not have short, light hair and a high forehead, this man that you say was Dusko Tadic outside the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have short, light hair and a high forehead, this man you say was Dusko Tadic outside the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: High forehead, that is true, just as I recognised him here, and his hair, yes, his hair was short and it, sort of, was towards the black. At that time it was lighter, but generally it was closer to the black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember giving a description of this man in January 1995 when you were questioned by the investigators for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I -- no, I again described him the same way as I did then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to look at a statement that you gave over three days on 6th, 9th and 10th January 1995, taken through an interpreter and an interpreter on behalf of the Registry of the Tribunal? Perhaps you would like to look at this statement in your own language? Your Honour, I tender it as Defence 31. I do not know if the Prosecution have a copy? They do, thank you. [To the witness]: This is a translation of that statement in your own language, but you were interviewed in your own language, were you not? I think that was not translated. You were interviewed in your own language, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, can you hear the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Were you interviewed in your own language at the time of giving that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with the assistance of an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You signed the statement that you gave the people questioning you. If you would like to look at this document which I tender as Defence Exhibit 31B and the other one will be 31A. If you look at the back of that document which has just been placed before you, you will see your signature on a witness acknowledgment dated 10th January 1995 right on the last page. That is your signature, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you signed that you said that you were giving a true statement, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the statement had been read over to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would like to turn to page 7 of the statement that is in your own language, you will see a passage highlighted in yellow. What I would like you to do is to read that out loud in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "When I saw Tadic during my case he was wearing a camouflage uniform and a pistol. He had nothing on his head. He had light, shortly cut hair and a high forehead. I do not think he had either moustache or a beard, but he looked as if he had some kind of infection and his face was red. I did not have an opportunity to look at him or the guards from close quarters".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is the description that you gave then of the man you said was Dusko Tadic sitting with those guards by the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A man with short cut, light hair and a high forehead, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, just as I described him now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No facial hair, no moustache and no beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as facial hair is concerned, the beard, as I said, maybe it was one millimetre long, maybe two or three, but why they wrote that he had no facial hair, that is their thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave that description to investigators for the Prosecution in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person talking to you read back that statement that you gave in your own language so that you could hear it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed a certificate acknowledging that, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only did the interpreter sign the certificate as well, but two investigators for the Prosecution signed a certificate. They were there at the same time, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the description you gave in 1995 when asked to describe the man you called Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you say in this courtroom now that he had a growth of beard of about one millimetre? Why you are saying that now and said something different in January 1995? Any explanation you can give?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible that I told them then that he did not have a beard because, in my view, when somebody is unshaven two or three days, for me, that does not mean that they have a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the facial irritation, the face being red?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as that is concerned, that too, that I only said it then only, but now I said that it was from the sun, but I could have given both examples at that time, whether he had some kind of an infection or it was from the sun, he was sunburnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These men also sitting outside the white house were guards at Omarska camp, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think two of them I had seen before there in the camp and I think that they were guards, and for the others, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a guard in Omarska whose name was Beka a guard with a red mark on his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went from the side of the white house to the other side and you moved the bodies, did you see Hakija Elezovic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he not lying down on the ground next to his son Salih?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went back into the white house did Hakija Elezovic speak to you and say you could have Salih's shoes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell Hakija Elezovic that you had seen Dusko or Dule Tadic at the white house on that day in Manjaca or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at Manjaca with Hakija Elezovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Hakija Elezovic again after that afternoon in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I only saw him this year, since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling the truth about this? Did you see him longer ago than this year and more near the time of your time in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him since the day when he was called in for the second time to interrogation. I never saw him until this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you went to Manjaca, did you not, after your release from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not released from Omarska. They transferred us to Manjaca in buses on August 6th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, but you went to Manjaca where you were still a prisoner for several months after you had been in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to Manjaca as a prisoner after you had been in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak there to other people about what you had seen behind the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not talk because in that moment it was more important how to find some bread to eat or some clothes to wear than to talk about it. It was not entering my mind at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hakija Elezovic knew you though, did not he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He would not get you confused with anyone else in the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that would be impossible for him to confuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, what I suggest to you is this. The man you thought was Dule Tadic of this description, you then told Hakija Elezovic that he had been there and killed his son Salih?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not tell him that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were wrong about the identity of that person by the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is why you described him that way in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this then. Senad or Sejad Sivac, do you know what the name of the person was, whether it was Senad or Sejad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Senad or Sejad, one of those two names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew this person, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not know his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I said his last name is Sivac and his first name is Senad or Sejad. OK, I can agree to Sejad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just one other matter to ask you about. Whilst you were in Keraterm camp you had seen a person called Zoran Zigic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen him on a motor bike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I tender Exhibits 31A and B. I have tendered them and now I offer them to the Court as Exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibits 31A and 31B will be admitted. Redirect, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Re-Examined by MISS HOLLIS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, the statement that the Defence referred to, that statement was read to you in your own language, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read, did you yourself read the English version of that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you relied upon the interpreter's reading of that statement to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said here that you described Dule Tadic to the investigators as you had described him here in this courtroom today. Here today you said he had hair that was closer to black, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as hair is concerned, it could be light, but maybe it was lighter from the sun. But his hair sort of went more in the direction of black.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Hodzic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. You may leave now. Thank you. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The next witness is the witness that will have distortion of his image?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So rather than begin with that witness, because we would have to take a recess in order to set up, we will begin with that witness on Tuesday when we resume. There are a few matters, though, that we can discuss regarding our schedule. You have four witnesses left, Mr. Niemann? I think four.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will just get my list, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You estimate we will finish on Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Four witnesses, your Honour, yes. One witness, Witness L, will take a full day I think.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand. The others each 1.5 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: With cross perhaps we will finish Wednesday, if not Thursday, I estimate with the Prosecution's case in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then from our discussion I guess earlier this week you had indicated that the Defence would be filing a motion to dismiss or a motion regarding some or all of the counts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You expected, though, that that motion may not be ready until after we recessed or adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that still your estimate

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is the case because we still have to wait to hear what is coming. There has been a variety of witnesses just at the end of the case, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We had agreed that we would recess for two weeks for the Defence to investigate to respond to the Prosecution's case, and the Defence I believe had suggested that three weeks might be better for you. We had not responded to that, the Chamber had not. What is your position regarding a three-week recess, Mr. Niemann? The Chamber is inclined to grant that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We are not in opposition to that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So we will stand in recess or adjourn for a three-week period after the Prosecution concludes its case in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When you file your motion the Prosecution will need to respond. We have a standing order that we use in these proceedings that allows each side 14 days to respond to a motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So I am wondering when you would file that because we would certainly want to have it and then have the Prosecution response before we return for our three-week recess, which means that you would have to file it about a week, no later than a week after we adjourn next Wednesday. So you think that is possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We were aiming to do it by the Wednesday of that week. That is how what we thought. Once the case ends it would take about a week to put together.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That sounds about right. Then will you want oral argument on that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We think it would be appropriate for oral argument.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It sounds like we can receive it just in time to give the Prosecution 14 days to respond to the motion in writing, and then schedule oral argument when we return from the recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you would keep that in mind in terms of your submitting the motion. Then can you give us an estimate at this time, depending upon how the Chamber rules on the motion, how much time the Defence will need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have considered this carefully and think it will be around about four to six weeks for the Defence case. It depends to a great extent on whether the logistics are successful at the Banja Luka end in relation to the video link testimony, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are still endeavouring, and I cannot tell you how difficult, we are struggling to accomplish that. As we had indicated, the rules do not call for video conferencing. They call for depositions by way of video. We have been attempting to resolve that request or to satisfy that request. I do not have an answer for you today. We are going to meet again when we adjourn tonight. We will know more next week and we will able to tell you more about that next week on Tuesday. So we will see about that. Is there anything else we need to discuss? If we go forward with the testimony of some of the Defence witnesses by way of video conference, we would have to develop some guidelines procedures for that. We have talked about it informally and we have received a proposal from the Registry. The Chamber will look at that and discuss that with you also next week before we leave you, before we lose you. So that even though we will be continuing probably to work on the video conferencing equipment trying to get it in place, I do not think it will be finally accomplished until after we adjourn, but if we can at least get some agreement between the parties on the guidelines to be used for the conducting of the video conferencing, the video conference testimony, it would help. Do you know the order -- without telling me the exact order, but do you anticipate that you would need the video conferencing equipment immediately when you were to begin your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think we will be starting with live witnesses. I have very left it in abeyance depending upon when it is in place so that, if necessary, we can go through all the live witnesses first to give still more time to accomplish the video link.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, is there anything you want to add at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Anything else Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are grateful for the endeavours everyone is making on our behalf.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are trying. Just in terms of the guidelines, we would suggest that the parties get together really and try to reach some agreement. There are some overall parameters, though, that need to be resolved and that would be whether Defence counsel would be there at the location present conducting the direct and whether the Prosecutor would be there conducting cross-examination, or whether it was your intent to use the equipment with Defence counsel being here in court. Which was your desire?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was our desire that as much of the proceedings should be in front of you as the Judges and the Defendant here and that the questioning should take place within this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Both from the Defence and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the Prosecution, yes. It seemed to us rather more satisfactory in relation to the conduct of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have done this before and it creates a problem because you have exhibits and you really do need someone there on the scene to handle the exhibits for the witnesses. I do not know whether the Defence may wish not to use exhibits, but it may be that in cross-examination we may want to put exhibits to the witness, and there are problems with not having anyone there at the scene. Also you need to have some means of satisfying yourself that the witness is in the room on his own and proceeding that way. The way we resolved it once before when I did it was that a represent of both sides is there, but in fact the examination is conducted in the court. So that the representative is there and if there are issues such as exhibits or any problems that arise on the scene, then a member of the team in Banja Luka can take over and resolve it at that point. But it is very difficult if it is all tried to be controlled from a remote locality.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As I indicated, the Chamber does not have too many, I suppose we do not have too many firm opinions about it. I can see advantages both ways, I suppose. If I were doing the questioning as a lawyer I would want to be closer to the witness, but then of course the accused is here. So you want to be close to the accused. But I do understand the concerns you have raised about the exhibits and that, of course, may work better if there is a representative there at the location where perhaps that could be handled, and hope that if we are able to get equipment that it is of such a level that you will still have the rapport that you may want with the witness. It may be a little premature. I hope not, because we are working very hard. If we can adjourn five minutes early, then we will have five minutes to get on the telephone and continue our effort. So, we will adjourn then until Tuesday at 10 a.m. (5.25 p.m.) (The court adjourned until Tuesday, 13th August 1996) 9
